summary.text: French Hill is the Republican nominee and incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 2nd District, seeking re-election. A Little Rock banker and former Treasury Department and White House official, he has served in the House since January 2015 and chairs the House Financial Services Committee in the 119th Congress.

paragraphs.text: According to his official House biography, he is a ninth-generation Arkansan who lives in Little Rock with his wife, Martha; they have a daughter and a son.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Vanderbilt University in 1975; his House biography says he graduated magna cum laude in economics.
From 1982 to 1984 he served on the staff of U.S. Senator John Tower (R-TX) and on the staff of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

Served as Deputy Assistant Secretary of the U.S. Treasury for Corporate Finance (1989-1991) under President George H.W. Bush, then as senior policy advisor and Executive Secretary of the President's Economic Policy Council (1991-1993); he received the Treasury Department's Distinguished Service Award in January 1993.

Worked in investments and banking for about three decades; he was founder, chairman and chief executive officer of Delta Trust & Banking Corporation from 1999 until it was sold to Simmons Bank in 2014.
Worked as a senior advisor to Arkansas Governor Mike Huckabee in 2008.
Civic roles include past president of the Rotary Club of Little Rock and 2013 chairman of the Little Rock Regional Chamber of Commerce.
Won the 2014 election to the U.S. House, succeeding Tim Griffin (R), and took office January 3, 2015.

In the 118th Congress he was Vice Chairman of the House Financial Services Committee and chaired its subcommittee on digital assets and financial technology; he has chaired the full committee in the 119th Congress.

As chairman, he led the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which became law on July 11, 2026 after passing the Senate 85-14 and the House 358-32, and his Main Street Capital Access Act (H.R. 6955) passed the House 270-155-1 on July 21, 2026.
